Give us a call and a member of the Mason Park team will walk you through your options and get your complimentary on the calendar.
Here is what to expect on the call, and why acting now matters.
We take down your situation and Dr. Cho reviews which path fits, from a single implant through to a full arch.
A no cost assessment with a 3D scan at our Fairfax Station practice, so you can see exactly what is possible in your case.
What can happen if treatment is delayed
Bone loss in the jaw, which can narrow the implant options open to you later
Neighbouring teeth shifting, leading to bite issues and more complex treatment
A higher risk of gum disease or infection over time
More extensive, and more costly, procedures further down the line
Dr. Cho obtained his dental degree from Tufts University
3D guided planning with CBCT imaging, sedation options for anxious patients, and a lab partnership that means the finished teeth are designed with the same hands that placed the implants.
New teeth are a significant investment. We verify your benefits, quote any grafting or extractions upfront, and put your out of pocket figure in front of you before you commit to anything.
Is the dental implant procedure painful?

The procedure is done under local anaesthetic and sedation options are available, so you should not feel it. Some soreness and swelling during early healing is normal and manageable. Most patients tell us it was far easier than they expected.
Can I really get a new tooth in one day?
Sometimes, yes. Depending on your bone quality and overall health, a temporary tooth can be placed the same day as your implant. Your 3D scan at the consultation is what tells us whether you qualify.
What if I have been told I do not have enough bone?

Do not rule yourself out. Bone grafting, sinus lifts and alternative implant approaches make treatment possible for many patients who were told no elsewhere. A CBCT scan shows exactly what is possible in your case.

The implant post is designed as a lifetime replacement root. With healthy gums, daily care and regular checkups, implants can last decades. The crown on top may need maintenance over time, like any tooth.
When will I find out the cost of my treatment?

At your consultation, once the 3D scan shows what your case actually needs. A complete single implant, meaning post, abutment and crown, typically runs $1,900 to $2,800 at Mason Park Dental. Bone grafting or extractions, if needed, are quoted upfront.

Insurance often covers part of the treatment, such as the crown or an extraction. Our team verifies your benefits before treatment and walks you through the financing options, so you know your exact out of pocket cost before you commit to anything.
What is the process for getting financing?

We handle it at the consultation. Once your treatment plan is set, our team runs the application with you and brings back the monthly options it returns. Nothing is agreed until you have seen the numbers in writing.
Talk to the Mason Park team and get your complimentary consultation with Dr. Cho scheduled today.

What is included in the $189 new patient special?

Your comprehensive exam — a full assessment of teeth, gums and bite, including an oral cancer screening — digital x-rays, a professional cleaning, and a written, itemised treatment plan. It is the whole appointment in one price.
Is there anything else to pay on the day?

No. This is the whole appointment, in one price — not a loss-leader that turns into a quote at the desk. Additional services, where clinically required, are quoted for your approval before treatment begins.
What actually happens at the visit?

We look properly, with a comprehensive exam and digital x-rays using cone beam imaging and an intra-oral camera so you can see what we are describing. We explain what we found and write your plan down, itemised and priced. Then you decide — nothing beyond the cleaning is started on the day.

We are an insurance-friendly office and our team will help verify what your plan covers before you commit to treatment. A dental savings plan is also available for patients without insurance — ask the front desk when you book.

Can I bring a treatment plan from another dentist?
Please do. A second opinion here is free, and it is the quickest way to know whether the plan you were handed is the one you actually need.

How long does Invisalign® treatment take?
Treatment length varies based on individual needs. Some patients see results in a few months, while others require longer treatment.
Some mild pressure may occur when switching aligners, but discomfort is temporary and minimal.
Teens and adults with mild to moderate spacing, crowding, or bite concerns are typically good candidates.
Can I eat and drink with Invisalign®?
Aligners should be removed before eating or drinking anything other than water, allowing you to enjoy your favorite foods.
Many dental insurance plans include benefits that apply to Invisalign® treatment. Our team can help verify your coverage.
Will I know my treatment cost before starting?
Yes. A detailed treatment plan and cost breakdown are provided before treatment begins, and we offer flexible financing options to help make Invisalign® treatment accessible.
Will I need a retainer afterwards?
Yes. Retainers are essential to maintain your results and prevent teeth from shifting. A set of Vivera® retainers is included in your treatment.
